## Simple explanation

Hyperparameter optimization searches for useful settings—such as
learning rate or regularization strength—by training and comparing
models.

## Technical explanation

A search procedure evaluates candidate configurations using a
validation metric or cross-validation estimate. Methods include grid
search, random search, Bayesian optimization, and successive-halving
approaches. Search results are affected by noisy evaluation, budget,
parameter ranges, and the chosen objective.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Hyperparameter choices can strongly affect model quality and resource
use. A well-designed search can improve a model under a fixed budget,
but the search itself can overfit validation data and consume
substantial compute.

## How it works

Define tunable parameters, ranges, a search budget, and an evaluation
procedure. Train candidate configurations, compare their results, and
select a configuration using validation data. Keep final test data
separate for an unbiased final assessment.

## Practical example

A team can compare learning rates and weight decay values using a fixed
validation split, while logging each configuration, training duration,
and metric.

## Common misconceptions

- More trials do not guarantee better generalization.
- Optimization cannot compensate for a flawed evaluation dataset.
- A configuration with the best noisy validation score may not be
  meaningfully better than nearby settings.
